correctness.rationale: Every exactly-four-part partition has unique y1..y4≥0 with λ_j=1+Σ_{i=j}^4 y_i and size n=4+Σi*y_i. Expanding e2 and geometric sums yields the claimed integral F(q)=q^4P(q)/D(q) with D=(q−1)^6(q+1)^4(q²+1)^3(q²+q+1)^3. Independent symbolic polynomial manipulation verified the identity, P=[6,15,34,57,95,121,146,126,106,72,50,25,11], and constant residues 864,32,6,−12 against Φ1,Φ2,Φ3,Φ4, respectively. Each residue is invertible for p≥5, so numerator and denominator are coprime modulo p. Since D| (1−q^12)^6, binomial valuations give D|(1−q^(12 p^r)) mod p^r for p≥7 and D|(1−q^(12·5^(r+1))) mod 5^r. The quotient-degree argument proves pure periodicity from n=0, not just eventual. Conversely any pure period T implies D|1−q^T mod p and the primitive third/fourth roots force 12|T; at q=1+t modulo t^6, N(1)=864 is a unit, forcing p^r|binom(T,j), 1≤j≤5. In particular p^r|T, and for p=5 valuation binom(T,5)=v5(T)−1 forces 5^(r+1)|T. CRT yields the minimal general m formula. Verification code inspected; bounded tests are supplemental.
